docs.title: [GET] harmonic days
docs.text:
api/power-quality/harmonics/day

start and end date should have a time appended 00:00:00 and 23:59:59 respectively follows the enum conventions of phase

Follows the taiga wiki. This endpoint is very similar with the issues endpoint The same metric over/under limit is still done but the return shape is smaller

Which means this endpoint /harmonics/day can be seen as a simpler return shape of /issues, which is then a by-day computation of /metrics all endpoints run by the same metrics analyzer class at the back-end

docs.title: [GET] issues
docs.text:
/api/power-quality/issues

As defined on the taiga wiki

Calculation of issues is defined by the per day calculation of /api/power-quality/metrics. The calculation step is done per day on your start date and end date

So technically this does the metrics by day, and assess it based on a min < x < max range

As of October 16, 2026, this is the saved metric limits

    METRIC_LIMITS: dict[MetricEnum, tuple] = {
        MetricEnum.POWER_FACTOR: (Decimal("0.90"), None),
        MetricEnum.FREQUENCY: (Decimal("59.70"), Decimal("60.30")),
        MetricEnum.VOLTAGE_THD: (None, Decimal("5.0")),
        MetricEnum.CURRENT_TDD: (None, Decimal("8.0")),
        MetricEnum.VOLTAGE_UNBALANCE: (None, Decimal("2.0")),
    }

For sure some of these are wrong, so please review

follows the taiga wiki

follows the taiga wiki

docs.title: [GET] metrics
docs.text:
/api/power-quality/metrics

start_date and end_date are required to have time values on them, appending 00:00:00 at the start and `23:59:59' at the end would ensure a proper start and end date

NOTE: this is not validated on the backend if you passed a good start and end date

Response of this api is based upon the set metric enum

Packaged as direct METRIC: float, its mentioned like this on the docs because the generation of the dto is dynamic based on the enum

MetricsResponseDTO = create_model(
    "MetricsResponseDTO",
    **{metric.value: Optional[float] for metric in MetricEnum},
)

Optional[float] is returned. You may receive null as a metric value. Computations mostly follow the taiga wiki, information about it will not be included in this wiki docs.

Phase on the request follows the defined enum

if an invalid value is passed it may throw a generic error, not defined at the back-end.
